key_equations.content: Fifth-order EHA: ddot y = -(b/m) dot y - F_f(y_dot)/m + (A_p/m) P_L ; dot P_L = -(2 rho A_p/V0) dot y + (2 rho Psi(v_e)/V0) sqrt(P_s-|P_L|) ; ddot v_e = -omega_nv^2 v_e - 2 epsilon_v omega_nv dot v_e + omega_nv^2 (k_e u + v_e0)

key_equations.correction: Symbols are omega_nv and epsilon_v (not omega_e, epsilon_e). rho is the effective bulk modulus in Pa, not density.

key_equations.content: Error-coordinate state space, x=[y, y_dot, P_L, v_e, v_e_dot], Delta = Delta_bar + eta, Delta=[0, Delta_2, Delta_3, 0, Delta_5]^T
mu(t,tau) = (1 + exp(-t/tau)) / (2 exp(-t/tau)) = (exp(t/tau)+1)/2

key_equations.note: The (A_p/m) mu x3 coefficient follows from E2 = mu e2 and is the anchor for the mu bookkeeping discussed in O15.

Delta_hat_i = - integral_0^t alpha_i sgn(e_i_dot + beta e_i^(q/p)) dsigma - beta e_i^(q/p), i=2,3,5

theorems.conclusion: All closed-loop states bounded; y and y_dot track y_d and y_d_dot 'in a finite time'.
theorems.time_property: The displayed Lyapunov derivatives are negative quadratic; the resulting estimate is exponential.
theorems.audit: Exponential, not finite time. No fractional-power inequality anywhere in the tracking part.

theorems.conclusion: Observation errors e_i (i=2,3,5) globally FTUB; |s_i| <= alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i) after T_i = |s_i(0)| / (alpha_i(|s_i(0)|) - sigma_i).
theorems.audit: Proof gap is the explicit assumption x_i_hat_dd = x_i_dd stated after (20); it is not guaranteed by (17) and, if true, would annihilate the very error the theorem estimates. Additionally (20) replaces Delta_hat_i_dot by Delta_i_dot without justification. (19)-(20) themselves are correctly printed.

assumptions: bar Theta_i >> alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i), with '>>' explained by the authors as 'much greater than'
theorems.conclusion: Closed loop (2),(16),(17),(22) bounded; y and y_dot track 'within a finite time'.
theorems.audit: Exponential convergence after observer convergence. The Case-1 inequalities use alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i) as a bound on the estimation error itself, which Theorem 1 does not provide (only |e_i_dot| is bounded, eq.(35)). '>>' is not a strict inequality and sigma_i is unknown. The interval t < T_i is not separately proven. Input boundedness is not a conclusion.

priority_question_answers.time_transformation_clock: absolute time t since t=0, with time constant tau; mu(t,tau) = (exp(t/tau)+1)/2; no terminal time T anywhere in the paper
priority_question_answers.tracking_error_actual_property: exponential decay of the transformed error; |e1_bar| <= sqrt(2 V5(0)) exp(-c5 t)/mu(t), effective rate about c5 + 1/tau
priority_question_answers.observer_finite_time_claim: stated as FTUB with explicit T_i; proof has an explicit unproven assumption
priority_question_answers.closed_loop_state_boundedness_proven: conditional on Theta_i conditions that depend on the unknown bound of |Delta_i_dot|

paper_measured: two chamber pressures (P_A, P_B) giving P_L
measurement_conditions.project_contract: position and two chamber pressures measurable; velocity estimated
measurement_conditions.difference: L03 additionally requires the valve displacement v_e as a measured state; if v_e is unavailable, an extra observer is needed and is not provided. L03 is fifth order (second-order valve), not a three-state plant.

state_ledger.note: x3_hat is structurally redundant because P_L is measured; it is used only to build Delta3_hat.

revision_records.original_report_claim: mu(t) = (1+e^-t)/(2e^-t); mu_dot/mu in (1/2,1); gains alpha_1>1, alpha_2>1-b/m
revision_records.paper_location: p.3 eq.(4); p.7 eq.(34); p.7 eq.(36); p.5 Lemma 1; p.6 Theorem 2
revision_records.paper_actual: mu(t,tau) = (1+exp(-t/tau))/(2 exp(-t/tau)); mu_dot/mu in (1/(2 tau), 1/tau); a1 > 1/tau, a2 > 1/tau - b/m
revision_records.impact: Numeric checks and gain conditions in the original report hold only for tau=1. Corrected throughout. The exponential (non-finite-time) character is unchanged; feasible gains now scale with 1/tau and the extra decay rate is 1/tau.

The reading of (19)-(21), (35) and of what Theorem 1 bounds changes: s_i is a sliding variable on the derivative of the observation error. A band on e_i itself would be |e_i| <= (alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i)/beta)^(p/q) (our reconstruction, not the authors').

revision_records.original_report_claim: eq.(19)-(20) have an extra s_i factor on the left; typographical error
revision_records.paper_actual: dot V_i = s_i dot s_i = s_i(e_i_dd + (beta q/p) e_i^(q/p-1) e_i_dot); left side is dot V_i, not dot s_i
revision_records.impact: Judgement withdrawn. The paper is correct here; the 'typographical error' note must not be cited again. The real gap in the same paragraph is the explicit assumption x_hat_dd = x_dd (see C9).

revision_records.paper_location: p.5 text before eq.(21); Theorem 2 on p.5
revision_records.impact: sigma_i bounds the disturbance DERIVATIVE. All Theta_i >> alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i) statements concern that derivative bound. Lemma 1's known bounds |Delta_i|<k_i are a different assumption and must not be conflated.

revision_records.original_report_claim: eq.(35) gives |e_i| <= |s_i| <= alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i), a neighbourhood bound on the observation error
revision_records.impact: No neighbourhood bound on e_i follows from (35). Moreover Theorem 2's Case 1 uses alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i) as if it were an estimation-error bound, so the robust-margin condition rests on something Theorem 1 does not establish.

revision_records.original_report_claim: Theorem 1 proof is not closed because linear terms are silently dropped
revision_records.paper_actual: The authors explicitly write that it is assumed x_i_hat_dd = x_i_dd

additional_corrections_not_in_review.item: mu bookkeeping is mutually exclusive between two families of equations
additional_corrections_not_in_review.detail: E2 = mu e2 forces the (A_p/m) mu x3 coefficient in eq.(5); hence eq.(8) must carry mu^(-1) (it does, per the page image) and eq.(9) must print (A_p/m) mu x3_tilde, eq.(10) must carry -(A_p/m) mu barE2 and (2 rho A_p/(mu V0))(barE2+Phi_1), eq.(23) must carry (A_p/m mu)^(-1) and eq.(24) the corresponding terms. As printed, none of these carry mu, yet (9)(10)(11) and (23)(24) are each internally consistent. Equivalently, eq.(25)'s printed -E1 term shows that (23) must contain mu^(-1), so (8)/(25) and (23)/(24) cannot both hold.
additional_corrections_not_in_review.impact: Two readings are stated separately in section 4.4 of proof_reconstruction.md. Reading A (eq.(8) as the controller): inserting mu in the three places closes the chain exactly, with no residual term - a pure typesetting omission. Reading B (eq.(23) as printed, used as the controller): the -E1 term of (25) becomes -mu E1 and a (1-mu) E1 barE2 cross term appears; once mu is capped by eq.(34) this term is bounded and can be dominated by larger a1, a2. Neither reading changes the exponential-convergence conclusion. Not a reversal of C7.

preserved_judgements: L03 is not a prescribed-time method: no terminal time T, mu depends only on absolute time.
Tracking inequalities are exponential / negative quadratic; there is no finite-time (fractional-power) inequality for the real position error.
Input boundedness and saturation are outside the theorems; saturation is left as future work.
Noise appears only in simulation (Fig. 7), not as a theorem condition.
The plant is fifth order and requires valve displacement v_e as a measurement; the project contract covers only position and the two chamber pressures, so the extra measurement requirement holds.
bar Theta_i >> alpha_i^(-1)(sigma_i) depends on the unknown disturbance-derivative bound and '>>' is not a strict inequality; the pre-convergence interval is not proven separately.
